text:
maria: FYI — after the cu12 bare-metal image rollout in ap-southeast-1 we're seeing huge provisioning slowness and a spike in container rebuilds. A bunch of nodes are stuck at 'Extracting' and Provisioner queue is backed up. anyone tracking?

jon: yup noticed. repro is: fresh bare-metal + cu12 image -> kubelet loops on pulling image, then container runtime logs show ld.so / modprobe warnings and NCCL peer failures.

ashutosh: can you paste the kubelet/provisioner logs? also which image tag did we push?

maria: image tag is redwood-runtime:cu12-2024-12-09. attaching snippets — small sample below.

maria: ```
Oct 18 03:12:01 worker-az1 kubelet[...]: Failed to unpack image "redwood-runtime:cu12...": io: read/write on closed pipe
Oct 18 03:12:02 worker-az1 containerd[...]: error extracting layer: lstat /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libstdc++.so.6: no such file or directory
Oct 18 03:12:03 worker-az1 kernel: [  123.456789] nvidia: NCCL warning: incompatible abi - unsupported symbols
```

kevin: interesting — sounds like some images were built against a different libstdc++/gcc variant. We changed the build worker toolchain for the cu12 -> gcc13 test last week.

sarah: infra-bot alert fired: provisioner-queue-depth > 500 for ap-southeast-1. infra-bot: "Provisioner concurrency exhausted, backoff in effect"

infra-bot: [alert] region=ap-southeast-1 metric=provisioner_queue_depth value=523 severity=warning

jon: also seeing a thundering-herd S3 download pattern — many nodes pulling ~6GB images at once. our egress bumped and cloud bills spiked for the hour.

ashutosh: We didn't prewarm caches for the new tag in that region. That explains the S3 burst. Could be causing timeouts and partial extractions.

maria: dmesg on one node shows ptx cache misses and then a module load order failure: "nvidia_uvm: failed to register range" then container runtime retries.

jon: quick mitigation: mark problematic nodes unschedulable and drain gradually so they finish rebuilds off the hot path. Also pause the rolling update to the rest of the fleet.

kevin: agree. we should pause the rollout immediately and add a rollback plan. If it's gcc/lib mismatch we can either rebuild images with the older toolchain or update runtime on nodes. Rebuilding images is faster.

sarah: downside: rebuild + re-push will re-trigger cache misses and another download storm if we don't throttle. we need to stage the rollouts and prefetch images to local registry/cache.

ashutosh: plan proposal: 1) pause current rollout 2) mark region as "provisioning-throttled" in deployer 3) rebuild image with gcc12 compatibility flag and push as cu12-gcc12-compat 4) pre-warm by pushing to edge-registry and triggering controlled pulls on a small batch 5) resume in 5% increments

maria: sounds good. can you run a small pre-warm job to pull to local edge caches? we have a registry in ap-southeast-1 with 200TB free.

ashutosh: I'll kick off a pre-warm script. snippet I will run: ```bash
for i in {1..50}; do kubectl run prewarm-$i --image=redwood-runtime:cu12-gcc12-compat --restart=Never --image-pull-policy=Always -- /bin/true; done
```

jon: also recommend adding rate-limiting to the provisioner so it doesn't start >N concurrent pulls per az. we want smoothing and backoff rather than a spike.

kevin: open infra ticket to update provisioner: limit concurrent_image_pulls=8 per-az and add exponential backoff jitter. This will help future rollouts.

srebot: [incident] created INC-2249: "cu12 rollout causes bare-metal provisioning backlog - ap-southeast-1" assigned to eng-infra.

maria: I'm going to annotate the bug with the dmesg and libc symbols. we should also add a compatibility check in the image build pipeline that verifies libstdc++ ABI symbols against a node's runtime.

sarah: ops note: billing alert already created for egress spike. Finance wants an estimate of the excess cost before EOD. jon can you approximate?

jon: preliminary: ~12TB downloaded across region at peak, ~USD 1.8k extra egress for the hour. will refine.

ashutosh: update: prewarm job started, 20/50 pods completed, local registry now has warmed layers for the new tag. queue depth dropped from 523 -> 120 in 10 mins.

maria: thanks. I'm pausing the rollout and marking nodes unschedulable. let's keep the throttling change as a follow-up PR.

kevin: long-term action items: - add build-time compatibility test (libstdc++ symbol matrix) - add prewarm step to canary rollouts - provisioner concurrency limits and jitter - document kernel module load ordering for cu12 images

jon: also add a note about NCCL compatibility checks and ensure we run a lightweight NCCL test in CI for each image tag to catch peer-to-peer symbol mismatches early.

maria: OK closing loop here. will update the incident and ping oncall if anything re-flares. thanks all :thumbsup:

kevin: :+1:

srebot: [update] INC-2249 status=investigating owner=ashutosh

maria: tagging product/ops to postpone any planned scale-ups in ap-southeast-1 until we have a stable rollout.
